target.title: fix(boundary-safety): guard response reads and UTF-16 truncation
target.body:
## Summary

- Resolve the current PR #97774 merge conflicts against `origin/main` while preserving main's MiniMax VLM success-response behavior.
- Refresh the boundary-safety full inventory to the current tree with 224 baseline-known entries, using only the required full-inventory update path.
- Keep the unique guard/baseline/tooling work intact and update the MiniMax boundary test to prove the preserved Trace-Id-aware overflow label plus the shared 16 MiB response cap.

## What Problem This Solves

The branch was no longer mergeable after main landed overlapping MiniMax VLM and response-boundary changes. The exact merged result could not be reviewed safely because the PR still carried older MiniMax test expectations and a stale boundary-safety baseline.

This repair makes the branch reviewable again by resolving the conflicts, aligning tests with the current MiniMax response-label contract, and refreshing the baseline to match the current source inventory without weakening changed-file enforcement.

## User Impact

Future provider/channel/runtime changes remain guarded against two recurring boundary regressions: raw UTF-16 truncation of user-visible text and unbounded response-body reads. MiniMax VLM keeps the already-merged 16 MiB success-response cap and preserves Trace-Id context in success-response JSON errors, so oversized provider responses fail closed without losing the diagnostic label maintainers already accepted on main.

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** The guard turns repeated provider/channel boundary review findings into a local source invariant. Users avoid corrupted emoji/surrogate-pair text previews and unbounded provider response buffering in new or changed production paths, while existing legacy debt remains tracked instead of silently expanded.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause CI/tooling guard plus focused conflict repair for MiniMax VLM response-boundary behavior and the full boundary inventory baseline.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local guard behavior, bounded `Response` stream behavior, MiniMax 16 MiB cap path, and changed-file enforcement. The remaining decision is maintainer policy acceptance for the baseline-backed gate, not an unknown contributor-side code failure.
- **Root cause:** The repository had canonical helpers for UTF-16-safe truncation and bounded response reads, but no changed-file source-of-truth guard preventing new production code from bypassing those helpers. The immediate review blocker was main drift that made the old MiniMax label expectation and 228-entry baseline stale.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` enforces the missing invariant at the source boundary: high-confidence raw text truncation and awaited unbounded `Response` body reads cannot be newly introduced in changed production files without being fixed or explicitly ignored with a narrow reason. Refreshing the full inventory to 224 entries aligns that invariant with the current tree.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not rewrite every legacy baseline entry, add public APIs, change credentials/configuration, change browser UI, or replace maintainer judgment about whether the guard should be adopted now.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` is the validator, `test/fixtures/boundary-safety-inventory.json` is the full baseline contract, `src/infra/http-body.ts` and `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts` own bounded response reads, and `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` remains the UTF-16-safe text owner.
- **Patch quality notes:** The default returns and catches in the guard are parser/classifier fail-closed branches, not runtime fallbacks that mask user behavior. Body-less response fallback paths enforce byte caps after reading buffered test doubles. Related PR scan: #100694 already covers the MiniMax cap on main; this branch preserves that behavior and keeps the unique guard/baseline work for maintainer review.
- **Target test file:** `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts`, `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`, `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`, `src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts`, and `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Raw UTF-16 truncation and direct awaited response-body reads are blocked for new changed production files; `--all --update-baseline` is required for full inventory refreshes; MiniMax accepts provider success JSON below 16 MiB and rejects/cancels oversized success bodies with the preserved Trace-Id-aware label.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A baseline-backed changed-file guard prevents new regressions without forcing a broad legacy cleanup in the same PR. The current conflict repair only updates the stale MiniMax assertion and baseline inventory needed to keep that guard reviewable on current main.

## Origin / follow-up

Follow-up to #97620. That PR fixed one bounded-read path; this PR keeps the broader boundary-safety guardrail that catches the same classes of regressions when future production files change.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- #97620 is the direct source follow-up: it fixed one provider response-read path, while this PR adds the repository guardrail for new high-confidence response reads and raw UTF-16 truncation.
- #100694 has already landed the MiniMax VLM 16 MiB success-response cap on main. This repair preserves that merged cap path and current response label instead of reintroducing the older branch behavior.
- The remaining unique value here is the boundary-safety guard, stable baseline contract, changed-check wiring, and representative regression tests. If maintainers decide the guard policy should be narrowed or split, that decision is now isolated from the MiniMax conflict.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The repaired branch is no longer carrying the stale MiniMax overflow-label expectation or stale boundary inventory. The current tree preserves main's `MiniMax VLM response [Trace-Id=...]` success-response label, keeps the 16 MiB bounded JSON reader, refreshes the full boundary-safety baseline to 224 known entries, and still reports zero changed-file boundary-safety violations.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw repair worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774`, branch `repair/pr-97774`, after `daily_fix.sh sync-main` onto current `origin/main`. The exercised behavior is repository guard execution plus real local `Response` stream handling in Vitest.

- **Observed result after fix:** The MiniMax boundary test first reproduced the stale assertion against the old `MiniMax VLM:` label, then passed after the test was updated to the current main label. The full boundary-safety baseline now matches 224 entries, the changed-file guard reports 0 new entries, focused guard/infra/MiniMax/image-tool/media-understanding tests pass, local changed-check passes on the repaired diff, and the local equivalents for the previously failing prod/test type and extension boundary jobs pass.
- **What was not tested:** No browser UI, remote MiniMax availability, or hosted CI success is claimed from local proof. Local single-shard `pnpm lint --threads=8` was not used as proof because `tsgolint headless` received SIGTERM without lint diagnostics on this machine; the same lint surfaces passed through `pnpm check:changed` and `pnpm lint --threads=8 --split-core`, and exact hosted `check-lint` remains part of the submit/settle verdict.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 — conflicting/dirty against main:** Fixed locally. The branch was synced with `daily_fix.sh sync-main`, conflict markers are absent, and current `pnpm check:changed` passes on the repaired diff.
- **RF-002 — preserve current MiniMax main behavior:** Fixed locally. The runtime keeps main's Trace-Id-aware `MiniMax VLM response [Trace-Id=...]` label and still reads successful JSON through `readProviderJsonResponse(..., { maxBytes: 16 * 1024 * 1024 })`.
- **RF-003 — guard gate / 224-entry baseline policy:** Disclosed for maintainer decision. The baseline is now current at 224 entries and can only be refreshed through `--all --update-baseline`; changed-file enforcement remains 0 new entries. Maintainers still need to accept the false-positive/noise profile for this new gate before merge.
- **RF-004 — MiniMax compatibility proof after rebase:** Fixed locally. The focused MiniMax test proves success JSON below the shared cap still succeeds, oversized success bodies are canceled/rejected at 16 MiB, and the preserved Trace-Id-aware label is asserted.
- **RF-005 — latest live check failures:** Addressed locally on the repaired head. `pnpm check:changed`, `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, extension channel/bundled lint, extension package-boundary compile/canary, and split-core full lint pass. Final hosted check rollup is left to the submit/settle path after push.
- **RF-006 — maintainer policy review plus conflict resolution:** Addressed by doing the conflict resolution and explicitly leaving guard adoption/noise tolerance as maintainer policy review rather than presenting it as a narrow code-only repair.

## Regression Test Plan

- `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts` locks guard detection, full-inventory baseline updates, changed-file behavior, JSON output, and false-positive boundaries.
- `test/fixtures/boundary-safety-inventory.json` is the current full inventory contract: 224 baseline-known entries after the sync.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts` locks the shared 16 MiB success-response cap, oversized-body cancellation, and the preserved Trace-Id-aware overflow label.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` keep MiniMax caller tests on real `Response` bodies so the bounded reader path is exercised.
- `src/infra/http-error-body.test.ts` and `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts` keep the response-snippet and bounded-body helper contracts covered.
- `pnpm check:changed` covers the current changed-file lanes for conflict markers, package guardrails, typecheck, lint, boundary-safety guard, import cycles, and related repository guards.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** CI/tooling, security-boundary, provider compatibility, message-delivery text boundaries, auth-provider response reads, session-state text previews, and availability of the new local check path.
- **Risk explanation:** The PR adds a new baseline-backed guard that can fail future changed-file checks when production code introduces high-confidence raw UTF-16 truncation or unbounded awaited response-body reads. It also preserves the MiniMax success-response behavior already on main: provider success JSON above 16 MiB fails closed instead of buffering indefinitely.
- **Why acceptable:** The guard fails with actionable guidance to use `truncateUtf16Safe`, `sliceUtf16Safe`, `readResponseWithLimit`, `readResponseTextSnippet`, `readProviderJsonResponse`, or a narrow `boundary-safety-ignore` reason for proven false positives. Existing debt remains baseline-known at 224 entries, changed-file enforcement reports 0 new entries, and maintainer policy review is explicitly requested for adopting the gate.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Guard adoption risk:** The PR adds a baseline-backed CI gate that can block future source changes introducing high-confidence raw UTF-16 truncation or unbounded response reads. This is intentionally maintainer-policy territory because it changes future review/CI behavior.
- **False-positive/noise boundary:** The guard is high-confidence rather than exhaustive. Existing debt stays visible in the 224-entry baseline, and changed-file enforcement stays focused on new violations.
- **MiniMax compatibility:** The success-response cap remains the current main/shared 16 MiB provider JSON cap. Oversized success responses fail closed instead of buffering indefinitely; normal provider-sized success JSON remains accepted under the same shared cap.
- **CI attribution:** Previously reported live failures were from the old conflicted head. The repaired local head passes the relevant local equivalents; hosted exact-head CI remains the final submit/settle signal.

## What was not changed

- No public APIs, credential/configuration behavior, browser UI, or remote provider behavior were changed.
- The PR does not attempt full legacy remediation for all 224 baseline-known entries.
- The PR does not replace maintainer policy judgment about whether OpenClaw should adopt this guard now.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` changes were made.

## Root Cause

The root cause remains a missing repository-level source invariant for boundary code: new production files could still introduce raw UTF-16 code-unit truncation or direct unbounded `Response` body reads even though canonical helpers exist.

The immediate review blocker was drift: main had already landed overlapping MiniMax success-response behavior and other boundary cleanup, so the PR's conflict result, MiniMax test expectation, and full boundary baseline no longer represented the current source tree. Syncing the branch, preserving main's MiniMax label/cap behavior, and refreshing the full inventory makes the remaining guard policy decision explicit and reviewable.
